questions.prompt: What does a language model do when it receives a prompt?
options: Understands the prompt's meaning the way a person does
Predicts the likely next text given the input
Picks a fixed reply it wrote for that exact prompt
Searches a stored database for the matching answer

questions.prompt: Which part of a prompt tells the model what task to perform?
options: Input data
Instruction
Context
Output format

questions.prompt: What does a low sampling temperature mainly change in a model's output?
options: It makes the model pick its least likely words
It makes word choices more predictable and repeatable
It makes the model's answers more factually accurate
It teaches the model new facts for the reply

questions.prompt: A user chatted with a model for an hour, then sends a new request containing none of that earlier text. What can the model use to answer?
options: A saved summary of the earlier chat
Only the last sentence the user typed before
Only the text included in this new request
Everything from the previous hour of chat

questions.prompt: Which prompt is most likely to get a useful result?
options: Summarize this article in three bullet points.
Summarize this article for me.
Give me a summary; you'll know the style I want.
Summarize this article, but avoid being too long.

questions.prompt: What is the main effect of telling a model to act as a nutritionist?
options: It works the same for any topic you pick
It shifts the tone and focus of its answer
It gives the model new nutrition facts it lacked
It removes the need to describe the question

questions.prompt: You want a model to label reviews as positive or negative, but it returns free-form sentences. What is the best first fix?
options: Add fifty unlabeled reviews so it sees more text
Add a list of product facts for it to memorize
Add two labeled reviews showing the exact label format
Add two recipe examples to show it variety

questions.prompt: Why ask for JSON with fixed keys when your program will read the model's output?
options: So the answer looks more polished to human readers
So the model will return exactly the same fields every time
So the program can parse each field reliably without manual cleanup
Because a clear task already sets the output structure

questions.prompt: Your first prompt gives a decent answer on one input. What should you do next?
options: Test it on several different inputs and revise where it falls short.
Submit it, since a first prompt should work perfectly.
Keep it, since a decent answer means the prompt is done.
Rewrite its tone, length, and format together to save time.

questions.prompt: A model answers a factual question in a very assured tone. What should you do before trusting it?
options: Ask it to add citations for support
Trust it, since the tone shows expertise
Accept it, since it sounds certain
Verify the claim against a reliable source
